items.prompt: A latch in combinational RTL usually means…
choices: The output can hold its previous value when inputs change
Every input combination drives the output every cycle
The module has no sensitivity list
items.explain: Incomplete assignment paths let synthesis infer storage to keep the old value.

items.prompt: assign Y = S ? D1 : D0; is latch-free because…
choices: Every input combination has a defined Y
assign only works on reg outputs
D0 and D1 must be constants
items.explain: Continuous assign is purely combinational—no path leaves Y unassigned.

items.prompt: always @(*) if (S) Y = D1; with no else…
choices: Y may not be assigned when S=0 → latch risk
items.explain: When S is false, Y has no assignment path—tools may infer a latch.

items.prompt: A case statement without default can infer a latch the same way a missing else can.
items.explain: Any uncovered input combination leaves outputs without a defined assignment.
